_meta.description: Question bank for InterviewPlan generation (docs/resume-interview-spec.md §4.3). Keys map to InterviewPlan fields: behavioral -> behavioralQuestions, technical -> technicalQuestions, role -> roleQuestions, questionsToAsk -> questionsToAsk. Generic, not tied to any real company. Technical questions are tagged with normalized skill terms from skill-aliases.json.
selectionRules: Pick at least 3 behavioral questions, preferring competencies the listing mentions (e.g. 'communication', 'detail-oriented').
Pick at least 1 technical question per required skill the user HAS, so they can prepare to show it.
Pick at least 1 technical question per required skill the user LACKS, labeled as a gap, with a 'how to answer honestly' tip. Never coach the user to claim the skill.
Always include 2 role questions and at least 3 questions to ask the interviewer.
Every STAR talking point must cite one of the user's real experiences (Rule R1).

starGuide.summary: STAR is a way to structure answers to behavioral questions: Situation, Task, Action, Result.

steps.name: Situation
steps.prompt: Where and when was this? Give just enough context (1–2 sentences).
steps.tip: Pick a real, specific moment — not 'I usually...'.

steps.name: Task
steps.prompt: What were you responsible for, or what problem needed solving?
steps.tip: Make your own role clear, especially in team projects.

steps.name: Action
steps.prompt: What did YOU do, step by step?
steps.tip: Use 'I', not 'we'. This should be the longest part.

steps.name: Result
steps.prompt: What happened because of your actions? What did you learn?
steps.tip: Use real numbers only if you know them. 'I don't have exact numbers, but...' is fine and honest.

feedbackHeuristics.description: Simple, deterministic checks for practice-mode feedback (template generator). An LLM may add more, but must keep the disclaimer.

lengthRules.note: Your answer is quite short. Add more detail about what you did and what happened.
Your answer is long. Try to cut the Situation down and focus on Action and Result.

weakPhrases.note: You said 'we' a lot. Interviewers want to know what YOU did — try 'I'.
It's okay not to know. Try: 'I haven't done that yet, but here's how I'd approach it...'

feedbackHeuristics.disclaimer: Practice feedback only. This does not predict whether you will be hired.

behavioral.text: Tell me about a time you worked on a team to complete a project.
behavioral.whyAsked: Checks how you collaborate and what role you take on a team.

behavioral.text: Describe a time a teammate wasn't doing their share. What did you do?
behavioral.whyAsked: Checks how you handle uneven effort without blaming others.

behavioral.text: Tell me about a time you disagreed with someone. How did you resolve it?
behavioral.whyAsked: Checks whether you can disagree respectfully and find a solution.

behavioral.text: Tell me about a time you dealt with an upset customer or client.
behavioral.whyAsked: Checks patience and problem-solving under pressure.

behavioral.text: Tell me about a mistake you made. What did you learn from it?
behavioral.whyAsked: Checks honesty and whether you learn from setbacks.

behavioral.text: Describe a time you had to balance several deadlines at once.
behavioral.whyAsked: Checks how you prioritize — important for students working and studying.

behavioral.text: Tell me about something you did that went beyond what was asked of you.
Tell me about a time you helped train or guide someone.
behavioral.whyAsked: Checks informal leadership; you don't need a manager title to answer.

behavioral.text: Tell me about a time you had to learn a new tool or skill quickly.
behavioral.whyAsked: Interns learn constantly; this checks how you approach new things.

behavioral.text: Describe a time when being accurate or detail-oriented really mattered.
behavioral.whyAsked: Checks care with data, money, or records.

behavioral.text: Tell me about a time you explained something complicated to someone without your background.
behavioral.whyAsked: Checks whether you can make ideas clear to non-experts.

behavioral.text: Tell me about a time you were under pressure. How did you handle it?
behavioral.whyAsked: Checks composure and planning when things get busy.

technical.text: What is the difference between WHERE and HAVING in SQL?
technical.whyAsked: Basic check that you understand filtering before and after grouping.

technical.text: Explain an INNER JOIN vs a LEFT JOIN with an example.
technical.whyAsked: Joins are used in almost every analyst query.

technical.text: How would you find the top 5 products by sales last month from a sales table?
technical.whyAsked: Checks if you can turn a business question into a query.

technical.text: What's the difference between a list and a dictionary in Python? When would you use each?
Walk me through how you'd read a CSV file and calculate a total for one column.
technical.whyAsked: Common first task for analyst interns.

technical.text: How would you use a pivot table to summarize data?
technical.whyAsked: Pivot tables are a core Excel skill for operations and analytics.

technical.text: When would you use XLOOKUP or VLOOKUP?
technical.whyAsked: Checks if you can combine data from two sheets.

technical.text: Tell me about a dashboard you built. Who was it for and what decisions did it support?
technical.whyAsked: Checks if you design dashboards for an audience, not just make charts.

technical.text: How do you choose which chart type to use for a given piece of data?
What is a branch in Git, and why would you use one?
What is the difference between an interface and an abstract class in Java?
What is a container, and why would a team use Kubernetes to run containers?
When would you use a hash map instead of an array?
How would you tell whether a change to a website actually improved sales?
If three volunteers cancel on the morning of an event, how would you handle it?
technical.whyAsked: Checks practical coordination and calm problem-solving.

technical.text: What metrics would you look at to understand website traffic?
What are a few things that help a web page rank higher in search results?
Write a one-sentence description of a study app for high-school students.

gapAnswerTip: If you haven't used this skill yet, say so honestly. Then mention the closest thing you HAVE done and how you'd learn it — for example: 'I haven't used Kubernetes yet, but I've used Git and Python on projects, and I'm working through a beginner tutorial.' Never claim experience you don't have.

role.text: Why are you interested in this internship?
role.whyAsked: Checks that you read the listing and have a real reason.

role.text: What do you know about what our team does?
role.whyAsked: Checks preparation. Answer only from the listing and what you've verified on the company's own website.
Usually the first question. Aim for 60–90 seconds.

role.text: What skill do you hope to build in this internship?
role.whyAsked: Checks self-awareness and fit with what the role teaches.

role.text: What is your availability during the internship?
role.whyAsked: Logistics; be honest about class and work schedules.

questionsToAsk: What does a typical week look like for an intern on this team?
What would a successful internship look like to you at the end of the summer?
Who would I be working with most closely?
What tools or skills should I brush up on before starting?
How do interns get feedback during the internship?
What do you enjoy most about working here?
What are the next steps in the interview process?
